claim: PARP family enzymes catalyze ADP-ribosylation through covalent transfer of ADP-ribose from NAD+ onto amino acid residues.
source: Members of the poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) family of enzymes catalyze ADP-ribosylation (ADPRylation), a posttranslational modification of proteins, through covalent transfer of ADP-ribose (ADPR) from β-nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) onto a variety of amino acid residues, including glutamate, aspartate, and serine (Gibson and Kraus, 2012; Gupte et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature

claim: ADP-ribosylation can occur as mono(ADP-ribose) (MAR).
source: ADPRylation can occur as a single ADP-ribose (i.e. mono(ADP-ribose), [MAR]) or multiple ADP-ribose moieties (i.e. poly(ADP-ribose), [PAR]) (Gibson and Kraus, 2012; O'Sullivan et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature

claim: ADP-ribosylation can occur as poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR).

evidence: Supported by citations to established literature

claim: MAR and PAR modifications are reversible.
source: Both MAR and PAR modifications are reversible and can be removed by a variety of ADPR hydrolases (O'Sullivan et al., 2019; Rack et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature
